forgexSolutions.name: Revenue Leak Check
forgexSolutions.description: One-week audit ($500 fixed price, credited toward any fix ordered within 30 days) to measure how many calls, web leads, and $89 consultation requests across both published phone numbers and after-hours windows slip through or fail to convert.
forgexSolutions.problem: Potential lead and call leakage across multiple phone numbers ([redacted] and [redacted]), unfinished website conversion flows, and after-hours emergency inquiries.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: While the company already hosts its site on a platform that supports lead tracking (leadconnectorhq.com), the unfinished pages suggest the platform's tracking and automation workflows may not be fully audited or connected to actual job conversion outcomes.

forgexSolutions.name: Lead-to-job pipeline
forgexSolutions.description: Automated pipeline ($1,800 setup plus $149/month) ensuring every lead from web forms, online booking, and both phone lines gets an instant reply and lands in their field-service or dispatch system within two minutes.
forgexSolutions.problem: Potential manual re-entry or delayed follow-up between the website CRM and field-service scheduling software.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: Web-marketing CRMs typically do not sync natively out-of-the-box with specialized electrical field-service dispatch and estimating software without custom webhook/API bridging.

forgexSolutions.name: Owner's Monday numbers
forgexSolutions.description: Automated weekly one-page summary ($1,200 setup plus $99/month) delivering booked revenue, close rate, average ticket, cost per booked job by lead source, and accounts receivable.
forgexSolutions.problem: Potential fragmentation of lead data, job revenue, and accounting receivables across separate tools.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: Requires cross-system data aggregation across ad accounts, the website CRM, field-service dispatch software, and accounting software.

feasibility.explanation: The website already runs on a modern web/CRM stack (referencing leadconnectorhq.com and services.leadconnectorhq.com) that supports webhooks and API integrations, making a Revenue Leak Check and Lead-to-job pipeline technically straightforward once the back-office field-service and accounting systems are identified.

aiDelivery.explanation: Deterministic workflow automation and API integrations should handle lead routing, instant SMS/email replies, and weekly KPI aggregation; AI agents can assist in classifying unstructured inquiry descriptions (e.g., separating urgent 24/7 electrical emergencies from routine $89 estimate requests) and summarizing call transcripts.

humanReview: Owner or General Manager approval of all customer-facing SMS and email response templates prior to activation.
Dispatcher review of any emergency or safety-critical electrical inquiries (such as panel hazards or power outages) rather than relying on automated triage alone.
Verification of mapping rules before writing customer or job records into field-service or accounting software.

risks.description: Automated SMS and voice follow-ups must strictly adhere to TCPA opt-in and opt-out rules, even though the contact form already includes an SMS/email consent checkbox.
Misclassifying a 24/7 emergency electrical call or live-wire hazard as a routine consultation could delay urgent response and create safety or liability issues.
Customer contact details, service addresses, and payment/financing references must be handled with least-privilege API credentials and never exposed in unencrypted logs.

commercial.value: Illustrative consultation fee recovery of $178 to $445 per month ($2,136 to $5,340 per year) in onsite consultation fees alone (2 to 5 recovered consultations per month × $89 published consultation fee), before counting downstream installation or repair revenue if hired.
commercial.implementationCost: $500 fixed price for the initial Revenue Leak Check (credited in full toward any fix ordered within 30 days); if needed afterward, $1,800 setup plus $149/month for the Lead-to-job pipeline or $1,200 setup plus $99/month for Owner's Monday numbers.
assumptions: Uses the site's only published price: $89 for a 30-minute onsite consultation in the Treasure Valley (which is credited toward the final bill if the customer hires AMP Electric).
Assumes 2 to 5 additional inquiries per month are captured and converted into paid $89 onsite consultations through faster response and unified call/form tracking.
Excludes project installation or repair ticket values (such as panel upgrades, EV chargers, or backup generators) because project prices are not published on the website.

discovery.outreachSubject: Quick question on AMP Electric's website & lead routing
discovery.outreachBody:
Hi [redacted],

I was looking through AMP Electric's website (https://amp240v.com/) and noticed a couple of small items on your live pages that might be affecting incoming inquiries:

1. Your Financing page (/electrician-with-financing) still has 'Lorem ipsum' placeholder text under the application steps.
2. Your Services page (/electrical-services) asks customers to call [redacted] in the text while the rest of the site lists [redacted], and references a list of smart-home brands below that isn't showing up.

Because your site already uses a modern CRM setup for online booking and text/email notifications, you may already have most of the tools you need in place. However, when a site setup is left partway finished by an agency or builder, we often find that missed-call follow-ups, after-hours emergency inquiries, or handoffs into field-service software have silent gaps too.

At ForgeX, we run a fixed-price Revenue Leak Check ($500, credited in full if you ask us to build any fix within 30 days) where we audit one week of calls, web forms, and $89 consultation requests to see if anything is slipping through—or confirm that your current system is already catching everything.

If it would be helpful to compare notes on how your current setup is working, just reply to this email or let me know a good time for a brief call.

Best regards,

[Founder Name]
[Founder Title], ForgeX
[ForgeX Phone Number]
[ForgeX Physical Postal Address]

If you prefer not to receive future emails from us, simply reply with "unsubscribe" or use [Opt-Out Link/Instructions] and we will remove you immediately.

limitations: Exact employee headcount (whether within ForgeX's 10-to-75 staff target range) is not stated on the website.
Whether AMP Electric currently pays for leads or digital advertising cannot be confirmed from the website alone.
The website obfuscates the email address behind Cloudflare email protection ([email protected]), leaving phone and web form as the only directly readable contact channels.
Specific field-service management and accounting software used internally behind the website cannot be observed from public pages.
State electrical contractor license numbers are not displayed on the website.

qualification.rationale: AMP Electric is an established, owner-led residential and commercial electrical contractor in Nampa, Idaho (operating since 1996, led by Owner [redacted] and General Manager [redacted]). While public pages show factual website maintenance oversights—such as 'Lorem ipsum' placeholder text on the financing page and two different phone numbers on the services page—the company already uses a CRM/booking platform (referencing leadconnectorhq.com) with online scheduling and SMS/email opt-in. Because internal lead-handling problems, staff count (10–75), and paid lead spend are unconfirmed hypotheses rather than verified facts, 'pursue later' is the appropriate qualification.
